text:
karla: FYI customer AcmeApps just opened an escalation — they see a spike in latency and a bunch of 401s starting ~09:12 UTC. They say most traffic is being routed to eu-west when they expect us-east (dedicated pool).
matt: can you paste a sample request id + headers? also which API (generation/embeddings) and model?
karla: sample request id: req_0a9f3c. model: gptj-redwood-7b, endpoint: /v1/generate. headers from client: `x-customer-region: us-east-1`, `authorization: Bearer <redacted>`, `x-request-id: req_0a9f3c`. Response headers show `x-served-region: eu-west-1` and `x-auth-status: 401`.
jess: customer reported billing jump too? that's concerning — could be repeated retries hitting fallback region costing more.
olive-cs: yep billing spike + unhappy execs, they provided a csv of ~2k request ids with eu-west responses.
matt: curious — did they recently edit a failover policy? any UI changes?
karla: they said they updated a routing policy via Console last night around 02:00 UTC. gave me this policy snippet they pasted:

```json
{"failover": [{"region": "eu-west-1", "weight": "0.0", "sticky": "true"}, {"region": "us-east-1", "weight": "1", "sticky": "true"}]}
```

karla: customer insists us-east should be priority but requests ended up in eu-west.
matt: looks suspicious — weights as strings and a leading zero may have been parsed unexpectedly. Also our Console historically used array index as implicit priority when `priority` not set. If the parser treats "0.0" as 0 and sorts ascending, eu-west could become higher priority.
jess: add to that: sticky TTL was 0 for the policy (I can see it in audit) — that means sticky affinity isn't preserving client pinning, so a failing auth in us-east would immediately failover.
karla: logs (from edge) show this sequence for req_0a9f3c:

```
09:12:02 EDGE req_0a9f3c client->route lookup -> policy eval -> select eu-west-1
09:12:03 PROXY req_0a9f3c -> eu-west-1 auth check -> 200
09:12:04 PROXY req_0a9f3c -> us-east-1 auth check -> 401 (token ttl mismatch)
09:12:04 EDGE -> client 401 x-served-region: eu-west-1
09:12:05 client retry -> route eval -> sticky ttl 0 -> picks eu-west-1
```

matt: interesting: we attempted us-east then eu-west? ordering is weird. can you grep the raw policy saved in control plane (`GET /v1/policies/<id>`)?
karla: control-plane policy raw JSON:

```json
{"failover_policy": {"priority_order": ["eu-west-1", "us-east-1"], "weights": ["0.0","1"], "sticky_ttl": 0}}
```

karla: but their Console UI shows a toggled priority with us-east first. So UI vs saved policy mismatch.
matt: that points to a serialization bug when saving priority arrays from the client. maybe our front-end uses 0-index boolean for `primary` and we invert on server. I'll repro locally.
jess: for customer mitigation — can we patch the policy server-side to enforce explicit numeric priorities? set `priority_order` to ["us-east-1","eu-west-1"] and `sticky_ttl`: 3600
olive-cs: please do that ASAP. I'll tell the customer we have a hotfix plan.
sre-bot: Incident #INC-2025-104 created and linked to thread 2150012345. Severity: high. Notifying infra-oncall.
matt: repro steps for infra: 1) take their exact JSON and hit `POST /v1/policies` via curl (include header `Content-Type: application/json`) 2) fetch saved policy with `GET /v1/policies/<id>` 3) confirm `priority_order` matches UI ordering. If mismatch, it's the serializer.

Curl example:

```
curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/v1/policies -H 'Authorization: Bearer <svc-token>' -d '{"failover_policy":{"priority_order":["us-east-1","eu-west-1"],"weights":["1","0.0"],"sticky_ttl":3600}}'
```

matt: I'll try to repro and attach server logs.
karla: customer asked for repro steps they can run — gave them a `curl` to hit edge and confirm `x-served-region` header. they saw eu-west 95% of the time.
jess: temp mitigation we pushed: forced policy override for that tenant to explicit ordering + sticky ttl 1h. Olive confirmed customer traffic now served from us-east.
olive-cs: they reported latency normalized and billing returned to normal baseline. thanks.
matt: root cause hypothesis: Console sends priority as UI index but control-plane incorrectly interprets string weights and uses ascending sort on parsed float, causing region with "0.0" to be considered highest priority. sticky_ttl=0 compounded the behavior by allowing immediate failover and retries.
karla: action items:
- matt: add validation to control-plane to reject string weights and require explicit `priority` numeric field (P0)
- eng-routing: add migration script to normalize existing policies with string weights (P1)
- console: add end-to-end test for ordering serialization (P2)
- customer-success: confirm no other customers changed policies in same window (olive-cs P1)
- oncall: monitor INC-2025-104 for 24h and check for regressions (jess P0)

matt: I'll start a quick PR to cast weights to numbers and preserve explicit priority if provided.
karla: thanks — I'll keep the customer updated and close the escalation once we see 24h stability. :thumbsup:
olive-cs: noted, keeping execs in the loop.
jess: marking incident acked. :white_check_mark:

karla: summary for thread: customer routed to wrong region due to policy serialization bug + sticky ttl 0; we patched tenant policy to explicit ordering and saw recovery. follow-ups assigned.
